knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

## Introduction

**R Markdown** is an authoring framework for data science that weaves together narrative text and executable R code into a single reproducible document. Using simple plain-text formatting, it can be compiled ("knitted") into polished HTML, PDF, or Word reports.

## Narrative and Mathematics

By combining prose with statistical notation, R Markdown keeps analytical explanations directly tied to underlying formulas. For example, a simple linear relationship can be written inline as $\alpha + \beta = \gamma$, or expressed as a standalone regression model:

$$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X + \epsilon$$

## Data Analysis and Visualization

First, we load the built-in `mtcars` dataset and inspect its summary statistics.

```{r summary_stats}
data(mtcars)
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")])
```

Next, we generate a scatter plot showing the relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

```{r plot_mpg, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg,
     main = "Fuel Efficiency vs. Vehicle Weight",
     xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
     ylab = "Miles Per Gallon (MPG)",
     pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
```

## Reflection

Using R Markdown is significantly more efficient and less error-prone than writing plain static reports. Instead of manually copying numbers and charts between RStudio and a word processor, knitting automatically updates all outputs whenever the data or code changes.
